residuals: Clock discontinuity: calendar timers follow realtime; a backward clock step postpones the wall and deadlines by the step (forward fires early, fail-safe for the wall). Not exercised (a clock step is a global host change).
A failed-cancel settlement tells the director; if a later replay then delivers the cancel, the core's own wake tells the director again (a duplicate notice, never a duplicate cancel or dispatch).
A timeout that is never acknowledged stays timed-out with waiting_on=director in status; only an acknowledged response deadline has an automatic expiry escalation.
The independent fallback cleanup timer is cairn's: it must be an explicit-UTC calendar timer (command in plans/README.md); the P11 one was --on-active.
L4a/L4b fixes rest on C (a clean stop lets systemctl restart start the failing unit); proved only in the live run.
Step-timer precision and ack latency on real seats are proved only in the signed live run; the live director fixture must run timeout-ack within 90 s of the deadline (tasks/ack.md).
